  PLANNING COMMISSION

  For the Regular Meeting of: September 16, 2025
Senior Planner:_________________________  Planning Manager:____________________________
  Rodrigo Pelayo  John F. Signo, AICP

SUBJECT: Conditional Use Permit (CUP 25-02)

PROJECT PROPOSAL/REQUEST: A request for approval of a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to allow
the sale of alcohol (ABC License Type 41 - beer and wine) for on-site consumption in conjunction with an
existing restaurant (Tacos El Unico) located at 2801 Firestone Boulevard, Unit B. The project does not
include site or tenant improvements.

Project Overview

  General Plan Designation: South Gate College District (Sub-area 2)

  Zoning: Urban Neighborhood (UN)

  Project Location: 2801 Firestone Blvd., Unit B

  Assessor’s Parcel Number: 6204-021-018

  Applicant: Jennifer Oden, on behalf of Fire & Shaw LLC / “Tacos El Unico”

BACKGROUND:

This item was originally scheduled for September 2, 2025, but the applicant requested a continuance to the
Planning Commission meeting on September 16, 2025, due to illness.

  Site Characteristics: The subject site is an existing dine-in Mexican food restaurant (Tacos El Unico)
  located within a two-tenant commercial building on a parcel measuring approximately 17,160 square
  feet. The site includes two surface-level parking areas, with the easterly portion shared with an adjacent
  multi-tenant commercial building on a separate parcel. The subject site is bounded by Firestone
  Boulevard to the south, Long Beach Boulevard to the east, and a mix of commercial and automotive
  uses to the north and west. The southerly portion of the subject building is occupied by a snack shop
  (Churrito Loco) that fronts Firestone Boulevard, while the northerly portion is occupied by Tacos El
  Unico, which is oriented towards the parking lot. A drive-through lane runs along the north side of the
  building, serving Tacos El Unico, with the service window located on the westerly portion of the
  building.

  The existing building measures 4,189 square feet and the subject restaurant occupies approximately
  3,220 square feet of its footprint. The restaurant consists of a 1,163-square-foot dining area adjoining
  the main entrance and storefront, a point-of-sale counter with condiment displays and beverage
  dispensers which divide the dining area from the kitchen and storage areas that are located at the rear
  of the tenant space, and restrooms also adjoin the dining area to the northerly portion of the tenant
  space.

(CUP 25-02) – 2801 Firestone Blvd., Unit B
September 16, 2025
Page 2 of 4

  Surroundings: The subject site is surrounded by an elementary school across Firestone Boulevard to
  the south, a convenience store and banking institution to the east, a used automotive dealership to the
  north, and auto repair facilities to the west.

ANALYSIS:

  Municipal Code Requirements for a CUP: Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC) Section
  11.21.030, Table 11.21-3 (Allowed Land Uses, Urban Mixed-Use Zones), the sales of alcoholic
  beverages for on-site consumption in conjunction with a restaurant may be permitted provided a
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP) is granted by the Planning Commission.

  Required findings for a CUP: Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.52.030, before a CUP may be granted, the
  Planning Commission (or the City Council on appeal) shall make all the following findings, as
  applicable to the property:

  A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of
  this title or the city’s General Plan.

  B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the
  existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the
  character or function of the neighborhood.

  Municipal Code Conditions of Approval for Alcoholic Beverage Sales: Pursuant to SGMC Section
  11.42.070, any CUP for alcoholic beverage sales shall include minimum mandatory conditions which
  are included in the proposed Resolution.

Business Operations

Tacos El Unico originally opened in the adjacent building at 2811 Firestone Boulevard in 1996 and
relocated to its current location in 2009. The business is currently operating seven days a week: Sunday
through Tuesday from 9:30 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.; and Friday and Saturday from 9:30 a.m. to 12:00 a.m. The
applicant is applying for a new Type 41 license from the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC)
in order to serve beer and wine to patrons as part of their dining service. Offering alcoholic beverages is
intended to enhance the dining atmosphere and improve the overall guest experience. By providing this
option, the restaurant hopes to attract customers who enjoy having a drink with their meals and appeal to a
wider audience. In addition, the ability to serve alcohol could contribute to increased revenue for the
establishment. Additionally, the applicant proposes modifying the operating hours to Monday through
Sunday, from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m. This would result in longer opening hours every day.

The applicant proposes to offer bottled alcohol as well as beer on tap. Bottled alcohol is proposed to be
stored within a refrigerator located directly behind the point-of-sale counter and the surplus alcohol
merchandise will be kept in a security cage within the dry storage area of the restaurant. The alcoholic
beverages are proposed to be served by the cashier, when a customer is paying for their meal. A standard
condition is included that alcohol may only be consumed within the enclosed building on premises. Alcohol
will be offered daily from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m., aligning with the business hours of operation. Staff
recommends a condition requiring the sale of alcohol to cease at 11:00 p.m., or one hour before closing,

  9

September 16, 2025
Page 3 of 4

whichever is earlier.
Security measures are not currently proposed; however, a recommended condition of approval will require
the applicant to install a video surveillance system to monitor the premises on a 24-hour basis and provide
recordings to the Police Department upon request. With the recommended condition, including other
standard conditions of approval, it is anticipated that the proposed sales of beer and wine will not cause
nuisances or compromise the public health, safety, and welfare.

To ensure adequate exterior maintenance of the site, staff recommends a condition requiring the removal
of all unpermitted exterior signage. Alternatively, the applicant may obtain permits to legalize existing
signage, provided it conforms to applicable Zoning Code requirements. This will help maintain visual
consistency and uphold the City's signage standards.

Additionally, staff recommends a condition requiring that all alcohol-related signage and advertisements
be displayed only within the interior of the business, away from storefront windows, and placed above
child-height eye level. This measure is intended to reduce visibility of alcohol promotions to minors and to
support a family-oriented environment consistent with the character of the restaurant.

Off-Street Parking

Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.33.030, the minimum requirement for a dine-in restaurant measuring less
than 4,000 square feet in floor area is 1 parking space per 100 square feet of gross floor area. That means a
total of 33 parking spaces would normally be required for the subject restaurant. The subject site is
developed with a total of only 23 surface-level parking spaces. Therefore, the site would normally be
considered deficient by 10 parking spaces.

However, the building and its parking area were originally built, and the restaurant use was originally
established, prior to the City’s 2015 adoption of the current zoning code. Since the number of parking
spaces (23) complied with the former zoning requirements, the current parking area has “grandfather” status
as a legal nonconforming use. Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.55.030(K), Nonconforming Parking, uses
that have nonconforming parking may continue in operation until the parking area is changed or the building
is expanded by more than 10%. Since no such change or expansion is being requested, the City cannot
require additional parking spaces as a condition to the issuance of the CUP.

CUP Analysis

In granting approval of a CUP, the Planning Commission shall make all the following findings, as
applicable to the property, as found in SGMC Section 11.52.030. Justification for each finding is included
in the proposed Resolution.

A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of this title
  or the City’s General Plan.

B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the existing
  and future land uses of the applicable zone.

C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the character
  or function of the neighborhood.

September 16, 2025

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:

In accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project qualifies for a
categorical exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing Facilities”, in that the
project will not result in any alterations or expansion to the existing buildings within the project site.
Further, no exceptions to the exemption apply; there is no reasonable possibility that the activity will have
a significant effect on the environment due to unusual circumstances. The property is already developed,
and the proposed use is the sale of alcohol (beer and wine) for on-site consumption in conjunction with an
existing dine-in restaurant.

DEPARTMENT COMMENTS:

Staff routed the project for comments to several City Departments including the Police Department, Code
Enforcement, and the Building & Safety Division. Police Department expressed concern due to the
business’s proximity to schools (Willow Elementary School directly to the south of Firestone Boulevard
and KIPP Corazon Academy schools on Long Beach Boulevard) and the likelihood of impaired drivers due
to alcohol sales. The conditions of approval contained in the attached Resolution include conditions based
on comments received from other City Departments, and are meant to mitigate impacts and improve safety.

In addition, the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control confirmed that a total of four licenses
are permitted within the census tract where the subject property is located, and currently, only one license
exists. Therefore, the area is not considered to be overconcentrated.

CONCLUSION:

Based on the above analysis, staff has determined that with the recommended conditions of approval, the
proposed project will comply with the SGMC, and all the required findings in support of a CUP will be
made.

RECOMMENDATION:

Based on the evidence presented, Staff recommends that the Planning Commission find that the project is
Categorically Exempt from the CEQA under Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing Facilities”, make the
required findings and requirements set forth in the South Gate Municipal Code, and approve the
application for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP 25-02) subject to the conditions of approval contained
in the attached Resolution No. 2025-08 and/or other conditions that the Planning Commission may wish to
impose.

  WHEREAS, the Applicant requests approval of a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to allow the sale

restaurant (“Tacos El Unico”). Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC) Section 11.21.030, Table
11.21-3 (Allowed Land Uses, Urban Mixed Use Zones), the sale of alcoholic beverages for on-site
consumption in conjunction with a restaurant may be permitted provided a Conditional Use Permit (CUP)
is granted by the Planning Commission; and

  WHEREAS, notice of public hearing was duly noticed on August 21, 2025, in the South Gate
Press in compliance with State law. In addition, a public notice was mailed 10 days in advance of the
hearing to each property owner, occupants and resident within a 1,000-foot radius of the project site,

and

  WHEREAS, on September 2 and 16, 2025, the Planning Commission held a regular public hearing
to receive public testimony and other evidence regarding the Application, including without limitation,
information provided to the Planning Commission by City staff and public testimony; and

  WHEREAS, Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code Section 11.52.030, before a CUP may be
granted, the Planning Commission shall make all of the following findings, as applicable to the property:

  (a) Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of
  this title or the city’s General Plan.

  (b) The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the
  existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  (c) Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the
  character or function of the neighborhood.

NOW, THEREFORE, THE PLANNING COMMISSION DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE
AND DECLARE AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1.  All of the facts set forth in the recitals are true and correct and are incorporated herein by
reference.

SECTION 2. Based upon substantial evidence presented to this Planning Commission during the public
hearing conducted with regard to the Application, including written staff reports, verbal testimony, site
plans, and Conditions of Approval (“Conditions”) attached hereto as Exhibit “A,” the Planning Commission
hereby specifically finds as follows:

  A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose
  of this title or the city’s General Plan in that the Community Design Element encourages
  the development of diverse and vibrant dining and entertainment options within
  designated commercial areas, which enhance the local economy and provide a range of
  services for residents and visitors.

  Specifically, Objective CD 2.3, Policy P.4 specifies that “the City should encourage and
  promote retail and service-oriented uses that provide opportunities to bring community
  members together. Such uses include cafés, restaurants, farmers markets, and theaters.”
  The addition of alcohol sales will enhance customer experience and is expected to
  increase sales. Thus, the approval of this CUP is consistent with the goals of the City’s
  General Plan.

  B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with
  the existing and future land uses of the applicable zone in that the restaurant is already
  an established business within a fully developed site, and the requested ABC license
  (Type 41) will not alter the existing physical structure or operations of the restaurant.
  The proposed use is consistent with the current zoning regulations and compatible with
  the surrounding land uses, which include commercial and retail establishments within
  the designated zone.

  The addition of the requested license will not introduce new incompatible land uses or
  development impacts, as the site is already operating as a small-scale shopping center
  with adequate infrastructure to support its current and proposed activities. The
  conditions of the CUP will ensure that the proposed alcohol-related uses are
  appropriately managed, preserving the compatibility with existing uses and allowing for
  future development consistent with the zoning district's objectives. Therefore, the project
  complies with the intent of the zoning regulations and the future land use goals of the
  area.

  C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to
  the character or function of the neighborhood in that the restaurant is an established
  business within an existing commercial property located in an area designated for retail

   and mixed-use development. The proposed ABC license (Type 41) will not introduce
  incompatible activities that would negatively affect adjacent properties or the overall
  character of the neighborhood. The restaurant’s existing operations are compatible with
  surrounding land uses, and the requested license is consistent with the site's long-
  standing commercial function.

  With recommended conditions of approval, including the requirement for a 24-hour
  video surveillance system available to the Police Department upon request, the proposed
  alcohol-related use will be controlled to minimize any adverse impacts, and the overall
  function of the neighborhood—characterized by retail, commercial, and community-
  serving businesses—will remain intact. Therefore, the approval of this CUP will not
  disrupt the established character of the area or adversely affect neighboring properties.

SECTION 3. The Planning Commission reviewed the project’s environmental impacts under the
California Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code Section 21000, et seq., “CEQA”)
and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 California Code of Regulations Section 15000, et seq., the
“CEQA Guidelines”) and finds the project to be exempt under a Class 1 Categorical Exemption pursuant
to section 15301 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines (Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code
of Regulations). Further, no exceptions to the exemption apply; there is no reasonable possibility that the
activity will have a significant effect on the environment due to unusual circumstances. The property is
already developed and the proposed use is an ABC license for ancillary alcohol sales in conjunction with
an existing dine-in restaurant.

SECTION 4. The Planning Commission hereby approves Conditional Use Permit (CUP 25-02) subject
to the execution and fulfillment of Conditions of Approval set forth in Exhibit “A” attached to this
Resolution.

2. The proposed project shall comply with all Federal, State, County, and Local laws and ordinances that
  may apply to this permit, stated herein or not.

3. The proposed use shall be conducted, and the property be maintained in a clean, neat, quiet, and orderly
  manner at all times pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code Section 5.08.020(A).

4. The approval of this permit, and the permit itself, shall expire if the entitlement is not exercised within
  one (1) year from the date of approval by the Planning Commission, unless an extension has been
  granted by the Planning Commission.

5. The permittee shall obtain the approvals, clearances, permits, and/or licenses required from City
  departments and outside agencies (i.e. County of Los Angeles Public Health Department, and California
  Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control) prior to the expiration of this entitlement.

6. Permittee shall obtain its City of South Gate Business License prior to commencing business
  operations.

7. Violation of, or noncompliance with, any of these conditions shall constitute grounds for revocation of
  this permit.

8. The sale of alcohol shall cease at 11:00 p.m., or one hour before closing, whichever is earlier.

9. Permittee shall install a 24-hour video surveillance system and have managers trained in how to access
  footage. Recordings shall be maintained for a minimum 72 hours. Police officers shall be allowed
  access to surveillance footage (during regular business hours) upon request for the purpose of
  conducting a criminal investigation.

 10. All unpermitted exterior signage shall be removed from the premises. Alternatively, the applicant may
  obtain the necessary permits to legalize existing signage, provided it complies with all applicable
  Zoning Code regulations.

11. All signage and advertisements related to alcoholic beverages shall be displayed only within the interior
  of the business. Such signage shall not be placed on or near storefront windows and shall be positioned
  above child-height eye level to minimize visibility to minors.

12. Permittee shall agree to maintain (and/or cause its landlord to maintain, if the permittee is a tenant) the
  property and all related on-site improvements and landscaping thereon, including without limitation,
  buildings, parking areas, lighting, signs, and walls in a first class condition and repair, free of rubbish,
  debris and other hazards to persons using the same, and in accordance with all applicable laws, rules,
  ordinances and regulations of all Federal, State, County and local bodies and agencies having
  jurisdiction, at permittee’s sole cost and expense. Such maintenance and repair shall include, but not be
  limited to the following: (i) sweeping and the removal of trash and debris as soon as possible but at
  least within 24 hours; (ii) the care of all shrubbery, plantings and other landscaping in a healthy
  condition and replacement of diseased or dead plant material with new material at an age similar to the
  material being replaced; (iii) maintenance of all irrigation systems in properly operating condition; (iv)
  the removal of graffiti within 24 hours; and (v) the repair, replacement and restriping of asphalt or
  concrete paving using the same type of material originally installed, to the end that such paving at all
  times be kept in a level and smooth condition.

13. If the application for this permit, or any conditions of the permit, violate the Zoning Code or do not
  fulfill the intent of the Code, the Planning Commission shall, following a public hearing, be authorized
  to take the following actions:

  a. Revoke the permit, revoke and reissue the permit with new or modified conditions, or modify the
  conditions of the existing permit as may be appropriate under the circumstances.

  b. Impose, as a condition of the continuation, reinstatement, or reissuance of the permit, a
  requirement that the permittee reimburse the City for all costs and expenses reasonably incurred
  in investigating, identifying, and documenting the violation, and in processing information
  concerning the violation for presentation to the Planning Commission, and, upon any appeal, to
  the City Council.

  c. This permit shall be revocable if the exercises of rights granted by the permit are discontinued
  for 6 consecutive months. The use subject to the permit may not be resumed of the permit is
  revoked; a new permit, including processing and public notification, shall be required.

14. The permittee shall agree in writing to the above conditions.

Mandatory Conditions

15. All alcoholic beverages, including beer and wine, which are sold on the premises shall be consumed on
  the premises; none shall be sold for off-premises consumption.

16. No alcohol sales displays shall be permitted that are visible from the public street or parking lot.

17. Employees selling alcoholic beverages shall be of an age consistent with Section 25663 of the
  California Business and Professions Code.

 Standard Conditions of Approval

18. The validity of the permit shall be conditioned on compliance with all state regulations and conditions.

19. All alcoholic beverages sales, offerings, and consumption shall be conducted completely within an
  enclosed building on premises.

20. The permittee shall be responsible for the conduct of all employees, including their education
  concerning Alcoholic Beverage Control regulations and provisions of the South Gate Municipal Code
  pertaining to the sale of alcohol (e.g., verification of age of purchaser).

21. The permittee shall acknowledge that the city has specifically reserved the right and authority to impose
  sanctions, including suspension or revocation of the permit, as a consequence of one or more violations
  of a state statute, rule, or regulation concerning the sale to or consumption of alcoholic beverages by a
  minor.

22. The permit shall be subject to compliance review of the property and permit conditions at Planning-
  Commission-established intervals; the first compliance review shall occur within six months of permit
  issuance or actuation.

23. The permit shall, after notice to the permittee and an opportunity to be heard, be subject to additional
  conditions to maintain or remedy land use compatibility, security, or crime control issues that have
  arisen since the issuance of the permit.

Building & Safety

24. Must obtain and provide Health Department approval.

25. All ADA parking must be properly marked and identified at all times.

26. All ADA accessibility signage shall be clearly and legibly identified and posted at all times.

27. Trash enclosure area must be maintained clean at all times.

28. All exterior common areas must be properly illuminated at nighttime.

Code Enforcement

29. Obtain all required permits for any unpermitted signage, including banners, window signs exceeding
  the 25% coverage limit, and remove all of the permittee’s A-frame signs located within the parking lot
  area.

30. Maintain all parking lot areas in a clean condition, free of litter, trash, and debris at all times.

31. Ensure that all garbage containers are kept inside designated trash enclosures and that these areas are
  maintained in a clean and orderly manner.
